EmailTemplate.subject: MLK Day: A Day On, Not a Day Off Blood Drive
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Hi <Name> Leaders in the <Black> community play an important role in helping the American Red Cross fulfill our lifesaving mission. As a leader in your community, I wanted to reach out to you today to invite you to join our lifesaving efforts to host a Red Cross blood drive in January in honor of the upcoming Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday.
My name is <Name> and I am an American Red Cross <Account Manager, Sickle Cell Account Manager, Area Booking Manager>.
The holiday is not only a time for honoring Dr. King’s achievements but also for promoting community service and activism. Many schools, churches, and organizations like yours are already involved in activities and community projects during this time, and incorporating a blood drive is another awesome way to commemorate his legacy by bringing the community together in the spirit of compassion, diversity, and unity.
The American Red Cross is also committed to compassion, diversity, and unity, and encourages eligible donors of all races and ethnicities to give blood to increase the diversity of the blood supply. One way we are promoting diversity is by teaming up with partners in the Black community to grow the number of blood donors who are Black because 1 in 3 African American blood donors are a match for people with sickle cell disease.
Let’s find time to talk so I can introduce myself and talk about hosting a Red Cross “MLK Day: A Day On, Not a Day Off Blood Drive” in January with your organization.
Sincerely,
<AM/SAM/ABM Name>
